evidence: src/infrastructure/logging/InfraLogger.ts: `export class InfraLogger { log(message); error(message) }`: a technical adapter that writes to the console with an inline `new Date().toISOString()` timestamp.
src/infrastructure/repositories/InMemoryTaskRepository.ts: `export class InMemoryTaskRepository implements ITaskRepository`: a persistence adapter built on the domain port, using `Map<string, Task>`.

src/infrastructure/utils/InfraFormatters.ts: `export function formatDate(date: Date): string` returns only the date part (`toISOString().split('T')[0]`). This is a different format from the logger's full timestamp, so it is not a duplicated rule.
The application layer injects InfraLogger directly (CONSTRUCTOR_INJECTS edge) and re-exports InfraFormatters. Both are layer-dependency issues and out of scope here.
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
This unit is the whole infrastructure layer, so it is normal for it to hold several separate technical adapters. Its three files are logging (InfraLogger), in-memory persistence (InMemoryTaskRepository, which implements the domain's ITaskRepository) and a small date-formatting helper (InfraFormatters.formatDate). All three are technical support code with no business logic, so the module does not split into unrelated concerns.

No rule is duplicated. InfraLogger builds a full ISO timestamp with `new Date().toISOString()`. formatDate returns only the date part (`toISOString().split('T')[0]`). They produce different formats, so this is not one formatting rule written twice.

No file bypasses the module's own abstractions. The repository uses the domain Task entity and the ITaskRepository port as intended.

Some concerns are out of scope for this rule. InfraLogger's comment says it should sit behind an ILogger interface. The application layer injects InfraLogger directly and re-exports formatDate. Both are dependency-direction problems, which another check covers. formatDate is a generic helper rather than an infrastructure adapter, which makes cohesion slightly weaker, but not enough to fail the rubric.
